FACT the file defines `putnam_2021_a6_solution := True`, so the goal is the forward implication: every 0/1-coefficient `P` that factors over ℤ into two nonconstant factors has `P.eval 2` not in {0, 1} and not prime.

FACT the first two conjuncts are routine. `P ≠ 0` because `Q` and `R` are nonzero, and `P(2) = 1` would force `P` constant, which contradicts `deg Q + deg R ≥ 2`.

FACT the hard conjunct is `¬Prime (P.eval 2)`. It requires `|Q(2)| ≥ 2` and `|R(2)| ≥ 2` for every nonconstant integer factorization of a 0/1 polynomial.

HYP that bound is the substance of Putnam 2021 A6. The known argument goes through root-location estimates for 0/1 polynomials (roots lie in the annulus with |z| < 2) combined with an integrality argument on the factor values at 2. Neither is in Mathlib in a directly usable form.

INFER the proof is not a short tactic script. Formalizing it means proving the root-bound lemma, relating it to `Q(2)` and `R(2)` as integers, and handling the degree bookkeeping, with no ability to test lemma names against the Mathlib sources (only compiled files are available). I did not attempt a partial proof, since the file must compile with no `sorry`.

I give up. I did not modify `/work/putnam_2021_a6.lean`, and it still contains the original `sorry`.
